Lemma
[Lower blow-up rate for finite-time singularities] Source: chow-knopf-ricci-flow:page-0253, chow-knopf-ricci-flow:page-0254 1. Lemma 8.19\group dilations-of-finite-time-singularities

Let $\mathcal M^n$ be compact, and let $g(t)$ be a maximal Ricci flow on $[0,T)$ with $T<\infty $. Then there exists $c_0>0$, depending only on $n$, such that \[ \sup _{x\in \mathcal M^n}|\Rm (x,t)|\ge rac{c_0}{T-t} \] for all $t\in [0,T)$.

Proof

Source: chow-knopf-ricci-flow:page-0254 \sketch Let $K(t)=\sup _{x\in \mathcal M^n}|\Rm (x,t)|^2$. By the curvature evolution inequality from Chapter 7,

\[ \partial _t |\Rm |^2\le \Delta |\Rm |^2+C|\Rm |^3, \]

and the maximum principle gives $K'(t)\le C K(t)^{3/2}$. Equivalently,

\[ rac{d}{dt}K(t)^{-1/2}\ge - rac C2. \]

Since $K(t) o \infty $ as $t earrow T$, one has $\liminf _{ au o T}K( au )^{-1/2}=0$. Integrating from $t$ to $ au $ and sending $ au earrow T$ yields

\[ K(t)^{-1/2}\le rac C2(T-t), \]

which implies the stated lower bound after renaming constants.

□
